subject: Lodestar PoC scope and deploy topology confirmation
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Vasquez <carmen.vasquez@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lodestar discovery — PoC scope & immediate asks

Thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side and the immediate asks so we can scope the PoC and validate SLOs: 

Key pain & goals (as we understood them)
- Inference variability: unpredictable tail latency when traffic mixes short classification and longer generation prompts.
- Cost pressure: need predictable unit economics as the product scales to ~200k monthly active users.
- Model fidelity: must match Lodestar’s current on-prem fine-tuned Llama-2-13B outputs for NLU tasks (intent + slot extraction) and the smaller generative prompts used for summarization.

Target SLOs you mentioned
- p50 <= 60ms for classification prompts (avg token lengths ~30).
- p95 <= 180ms; p99 <= 400ms for mixed traffic.
- 1M tokens/day steady state during PoC; burst up to 3x during marketing spikes.

Technical constraints & clarifying questions
1) Model variants: You said you have an L2-13B fine-tuned and a distilled 7B variant. For PoC, confirm whether we should serve both concurrently (routing by prompt type) or convert everything to the 13B.
2) KV/prefix cache: we’ll need a sample of typical conversation prefixes (10–40 tokens) to model cache hit ratios. Can you share a sanitized trace?
3) Auth & network: you prefer VPC peering for the private deploy; confirm whether IP allowlisting is sufficient or you require a full Private (air-gapped) package.

Proposed PoC deliverables (2 weeks)
- Baseline latency/throughput map (p50/p95/p99 across prompt shapes)
- Two topology options: Hosted with dedicated pool vs Private VPC small cluster (cost delta and failure modes)
- Runbook for cache warm-up and burst scaling; initial provisioning estimate attached.

Attachments: [Attachment: lodestar_poc_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

Next steps
- Carmen: share 48h of anonymized traces and clarify which model variant is required for fidelity checks.
- Lodestar: confirm acceptance criteria (latency numbers above or relaxations).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a short provisioning estimate and a mutual action plan (HubSpot HS-78902).

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Carmen Vasquez <carmen.vasquez@lodestar.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benjamin Cho <benjamin.cho@lodestar.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Lodestar discovery — PoC scope & immediate asks

Thanks Markus — helpful summary. A few clarifications below.

- Model variants: we need the 13B for NLU fidelity; the 7B may be used for summarization but only if output quality is comparable. For the PoC please prioritize the 13B and include a 7B fallback path for cost comparisons.
- Traces: attaching a sanitized sample of 72h traces (pii-stripped). Note the short prompts are ~15 tokens for intent classification and long ones up to ~220 tokens for chained instructions.
- Network: VPC peering + strict IP allowlist is preferred. We will not require air-gapped for the initial PoC.

Acceptance criteria (Lodestar)
- Classification fidelity: same intent accuracy within 1.5% of our local baseline.
- Latency: p95 for classification <= 200ms in steady state.
- Cost: unit token cost must be <= 65% of our current on-prem amortized cost for the duration of PoC.

We’ll aim to get the traces to you by EOD Monday and schedule the follow-up technical call for next Tuesday.

Regards,
Carmen Vasquez
Head of Infrastructure
Lodestar Analytics
[Attachment: lodestar_traces_72h.json (sanitized sample)]
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Vasquez <carmen.vasquez@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 11:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Lodestar discovery — PoC scope & immediate asks

Appreciate the quick clarifications and the trace sample, Carmen. Quick notes after an initial pass on the traces: 

- Observed prompt mix: ~67% short (<30 tokens), 22% mid (30–120), 11% long (>120). That distribution is favorable for prefix caching and KV reuse; we’ll model cache hit curves in the PoC.
- Cold start vs warm: there are spikes in tail latency that line up with low-cold-cache windows — our suggested mitigation is short-lived warm pools (pre-warmed workers) combined with lazy KV warming for the most frequent prefixes.

PoC technical plan (outline)
1) Topology A — Hosted Dedicated Pool (fastest onramp)
   - Dedicated GPU pool running 13B with autoscaling threshold tuned to p95 target.
   - Multi-model routing: classify -> route to quantized 13B path for NLU; summarization routed to 7B if fidelity tests pass.
2) Topology B — Private VPC small cluster
   - VPC peering, customer-managed subnets, KMS integration for keys. Slightly higher latency variance but stronger network control.

Measurements we’ll collect in PoC
- Token-level latency breakdown (token-level p50/p95/p99) and per-route cost.
- Cache hit ratios by prefix length.
- Failure injection run to validate fallback routing from 13B -> 7B and cross-region routing if a pool saturates.

Immediate asks from Redwood
- Sample inference payloads with typical prompt templates (you already sent traces — the payload examples will help us validate tokenization).
- Any compliance constraints for log retention or sample sharing (we will redact logs if needed).

I’ve attached a provisioning estimate (spreadsheet) and a short mutual action plan placeholder that we can update after your confirmation.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_provisioning_estimate.xlsx (XLSX)]

I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive for next Tuesday 10:00am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Cheers,
Markus
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Vasquez <carmen.vasquez@lodestar.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 16:20:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Lodestar discovery — PoC scope & immediate asks

Quick ops note from Redwood: wanted to call out tradeoffs so you have the options pre-synced before the call.

Option 1: Hosted Dedicated (recommended for fastest iteration)
- Pros: lower end-to-end latency, prebuilt autoscaling, integrated telemetry in Redwood Console, faster rollout for canary testing.
- Cons: less direct control over network path; requires VPC peering + strict egress rules.

Option 2: Private VPC small cluster (recommended if you need tighter network controls)
- Pros: customer-managed network, KMS/HSM integration, full control over ingress/egress.
- Cons: slightly higher p95 in our measurements due to network hop variability; longer provisioning lead time.

Operational items we’ll cover on the call:
- Warm pool sizing and safe defaults for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Cache warming strategy (prefetch top-5 prefixes per intent during scheduled warm windows).
- Rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback to 7B fallback path and cross-pool fallback.

If Lodestar confirms the 13B as baseline, we’ll prepare an initial canary run template and the parameter set for your infra team to review (FTS: warm pool size, batch thresholds, kv-cache TTLs).

— Grace
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
